newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks advance at opening.
newsitem.headline: French stocks advance at opening.

text.p: French shares opened in positive ground on Tuesday, continuing a rebound started yesterday after their Friday fright on Greenspan's cautionary note on rising markets.
Markets fell heavily at the end of last week on comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on the "irrational exuberance" of financial markets.
The CAC gave back some of the opening gains but operators were expecting the market to rise during the day, resuming its advance for the end of year.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 8.68 points or 0.38 percent at 2,264.52 at 0915 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,271.5 from 2,259 on Monday's close.

Some of the market froth has been cleared after the strong rise in recent weeks. "Institutionals sat tight, the activity was very much futures driven, with hedge funds fairly active," said one operator.
Greenspan's comments helped inject some caution and the market could move side ways for a while.
Brokers said electrical equipment firm Schneider placed two million shares in London on Monday at between 235-238 francs per share.
They added that Sidel also placed one percent of capital yesterday in London at around 340 francs per share.
Insurer Axa active, rises 0.47 percent to 299.1, spurred by year figures from Australian unit National Mutual.
Carrefour busy, up 1.55 percent to 3,214. A block of 5,280 shares changed hands at 3,220 francs per share.
Drinks firm Remy-Cointreau gains 0.73 percent to 138 francs, after posting first-half results seen not so bad as feared.
